source_caption:
Steven Soderbergh and Julia Roberts completely subvert the traditional legal thriller by turning the protagonist’s perceived flaws—her brash, unapologetic demeanor and fiercely working-class wardrobe—into her ultimate weapon. While the corporate lawyers rely on cold, clinical paperwork, Erin builds an unprecedented, devastating class-action lawsuit entirely through radical, genuine human empathy. Roberts’ Oscar-winning performance brilliantly proves that the most powerful asset in a courtroom isn’t always a pristine Ivy League pedigree, but an unrelenting willingness to fight for the exact people the system was explicitly designed to ignore.
⠀
Erin Brockovich (2000), directed by Steven Soderbergh, starring Julia Roberts, Albert Finney, Aaron Eckhart. A desperate, unemployed single mother secures a low-level job at a struggling law firm and almost single-handedly spearheads a monumental, historic legal battle against a massive energy corporation poisoning a local town’s water supply.

source_details.title: Erin Brockovich
source_details.synopsis: Erin Brockovich is a 2000 American biographical legal drama film directed by Steven Soderbergh and written by Susannah Grant. The film is a dramatization of the true story of Erin Brockovich, portrayed by Julia Roberts, who initiated a legal case against the Pacific Gas and Electric Company over its culpability for the Hinkley groundwater contamination incident. Erin Brockovich premiered in Los Angeles on March 14, 2000, and was released theatrically in the United States by Universal Pictures on March 17, 2000, and internationally by Columbia TriStar Film Distributors International.
